title: Getting your London Datastore API key

what: If you don’t have an account yet
title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: Click Create Account top right dialog. ’ll asked email address. Type email click Send signup link. Datastore email link finish setting account — open email follow link choose password. ’s done, come back data.london.gov.uk sign using login dialog step 2.

title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: ’re signed , small cog icon appears top-right page. Click choose Account menu. takes Profile page, lists account settings, including API key.

what: 4. Reveal and copy your API key
title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: Find API Key row click Manage. dialog opens showing key — string looks something like xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx (UUID). Click copy icon next key copy clipboard. Keep key safe. Anyone API key can act Datastore . Don’t paste shared documents, don’t commit Git repository, don’t share screenshots chat messages.

what: 5. Store your key so R can use it
title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: cleanest way use key ldndatar2 save environment variable called LDS_API_KEY. way isn’t sitting R scripts might shared accident. easiest place set user-level .Renviron file. R session, run: opens .Renviron editor. Add single line: Replace example value key just copied. Save file restart R (RStudio: Session → Restart R) new variable picked . can check ’s working running: R print key back .
code: usethis::edit_r_environ() LDS_API_KEY=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx Sys.getenv("LDS_API_KEY")

title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: can now pass key ldndatar2 function needs . example, download metadata private dataset: add new resource dataset :
code: library(ldndatar2)  metadata <- lds_download_metadata(   slug = "your-private-dataset-slug",   api_key = Sys.getenv("LDS_API_KEY") ) lds_add_resource(   slug    = "your-dataset-slug",   path    = "path/to/your-file.csv",   title   = "Your resource title",   api_key = Sys.getenv("LDS_API_KEY") )

title: Getting your London Datastore API key
text: Manage button nothing. Make sure ’re signed — email address shown top Profile page. API call returns 401 403 error. Double-check key copied full extra spaces, restarted R editing .Renviron. ’ve lost leaked key. Go back API key dialog (steps 3 4) use ⋮ menu next key regenerate . old key stop working immediately.

title: Intro to the London Datastore
text: ’re new London Datastore things need know navigagte package: Slug slug last part URL address serves unique identifies. example, URL https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/mps-monthly-crime-dashboard-data-e5n6w slug e5n6w. Datasets London Datastore, webpage referred dataset. example, Metropolitan Police Monthly Crime Data page dataset. can use lds_metadata(type = "datasets") function get information available datasets. Resources file London Datastore page (dataset) referred resource. example, Metropolitan Police Monthly Crime Data page csv excel files resources. can use lds_metadata(type = "resources") function get information available resources. Topics Topics group datasets resources subject area, helping users discover related content London Datastore. can use lds_metadata(type = "topics") retrieve metadata available topics. Teams Teams (previously called organisations) publishers maintainers datasets resources London Datastore. Examples include Office National Statistics (ONS), Transport London (TfL), Greater London Authority (GLA). Use lds_metadata(type = "teams") retrieve metadata teams.

what: Exploring the London Datastore using ldndatar2
title: Intro to the London Datastore
text: demonstrated , ldndatar2 enables users download metadata datasets, resources, teams, topics. functionality helps users discover resources may directly associated dataset name whose descriptions embedded within iframe, making difficult locate standard web interface. lds_download_resource() function enables users analysts integrate API calls directly workflows, reducing manual steps giving R users greater flexibility accessing processing data.

title: Intro to the London Datastore
text: ldndatar2 helps publishers streamline workflows automating common publishing tasks. example, recurring publications require regular updates description pages resources, ldndatar2 reduces need repetitive point--click drag--drop actions, via functions like lds_add_resource(), lds_replace_resource() lds_patch_description(). supports principles Reproducible Analytical Pipelines (RAP) framework enabling automated, consistent, reproducible publishing workflows. ldndatar2 also allows users search least recently updated datasets resources, helping teams identify stale resources track new publications.

what: Access London Datastore Data and Resources
title: Access London Datastore Data and Resources
text: ldndatar2 provides functions access download data, metadata, resources London Datastore. package updated successor original ldndatar package, utilising current London Datastore API. allows users programmatically catalogue, query, retrieve update datasets resources published Greater London Authority partner organisations.

title: Access London Datastore Data and Resources
text: can install ldndatar2 directly GitHub. package available CRAN. using remotes:
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("Greater-London-Authority/ldndatar2") # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("Greater-London-Authority/ldndatar2")

title: Access London Datastore Data and Resources
code: library(ldndatar2)  # Browse available datasets datasets <- lds_metadata(type = "datasets")  # Browse available resources resources <- lds_metadata(type = "resources")  # Download metadata for a specific dataset metadata <- lds_download_metadata(slug = "your-dataset-slug")  # Download a resource to your working directory (folder) lds_download_resource(slug = "your-dataset-slug")

title: Access London Datastore Data and Resources
